sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the appellant/accused under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C for setting aside the judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the VI Additional District and Special Judge,
Mysuru in S.C.No.263/2015 dated 14.3.2018, for having found the appellant guilty and convicted and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for 2 years and pay fine of Rs.1000/-, in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for 3 months, for the offence punishable under Section 366 of IPC and further sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of 10 years and pay fine of Rs.5000/-, in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for 1 year for the offences punishable under Section 5(i) read with 6 of POCSO Act.

opennyai_summary.issue:
8. Having heard the arguments and perused the records, the point that arises for my consideration is,
(a) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt, that the appellant abducted the minor girl, who is below the age of 18 years from the custody of the guardian and compelled her for marriage NC: 2023:KHC:25295 and seduced to have intercourse with her, thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 366 of IPC?
(b) Whether the prosecution also proves beyond all reasonable doubts, that the accused had sexual intercourse with the PW2, who is below aged of 16 years and sexually assaulted her repeatedly on her and thereby he has committed offence punishable under Sections 376(2) (i) and (n) of IPC and section 6 of POCSO Act?
(c) Whether the judgment of the trial court calls for any interference?
9. On perusal of the evidence on record, it is worth to mention the evidence adduced by the prosecution before the Trial Court .
opennyai_summary.20_July_2023__ANALYSIS:
There is no repeated sexual intercourse, to bring under Section 376 (2)(i) and (n) of IPC .
In the recent case, the co-ordinate bench of this court has converted the offence - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:25295 under Section 6 of POCSO Act to Section 4 of POCSO Act, as there is no aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the victim.
Considering the same, I am of the view the prosecution is able to establish the offence under Section 4 of the POCSO Act but not for Section 6 of POCSO Act.
Therefore, considering facts and circumstances of the case the Section 4 of POCSO Act provides for minimum of 7 years punishable to the extent of life.
opennyai_summary.20_July_2023__decision:
As regards to the sentence, the trial court convicted the accused only for 1 year sentence under section 366 of IPC and 10 years for 376 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act, the appellant is in Dinesha vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145739981/
6 custody from 22.5.2015, almost from past 8 years .
Therefore, the minimum sentence of 7 years imposed on Section 4 of POCSO Act, meets the ends of justice.

The judgment of trial court for convicting the appellant is upheld.
The sentence passed by the trial court convicting the appellant in respect of Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 2 years with fine of Rs.1000/- and in default to undergo simple imprisonment for 3 months, is upheld.
However the sentence of conviction of the appellant under Section 5(L) read with 6 of POCSO Act, is modified into Section 4 of POCSO Act.
The appellant is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for 7 years and pay fine of Rs.5000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) and in default of payment of fine, shall undergo one year - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:25295 simple imprisonment for the offence punishable under Section 4 of POCSO Act.
The appellant is stated to be already in custody since more than 8 years.
Therefore, the appellant is entitled for set off under Section 428 of Cr.P.C.
The jail authority is directed to release the appellant from the jail, if he has already undergone the punishment of more than 7 years.
